children: ‌co-founder Jack Clark said on Saturday that one of his company’s internal economic models projected U.S. economic output to reach $44T by 2030 thanks to fast-improving AI capabilities that could transform all fields at a more rapid pace.
He made the remarks at the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meeting taking place in Bangkok this week.

Clark called the $44T figure, which indicates a massive jump from the ⁠current U.S. economic output of little more than $30T, "sounds very outlandish,” but added that scientific discovery is expanding considerably due to AI.

The projection assumed "the technology continuing to get better," he said, adding, "And if ​GDP were to grow this ​much, ⁠then economic doctrine suggests that new industries and inventions would need ⁠to ​have been created ​to power such a major economic expansion."
Additionally, Clark underscored the need for international cooperation to establish "unusual and serious ​rules" for the transformative technology.

"We should expect that in the coming years, the whole pace of progress of not just AI but science as a whole will speed up, and this will feel confusing and disorienting, and will bring with it great wealth and potentially ​great peril," said Clark, who serves as Anthropic's "head of public benefit."

"Being able to use AI for science opens us up to the ​misuses of science as well, biological and cyber weapons and things we cannot yet imagine, and we have ​many choices to make," he added, according to Reuters.
